selectionCriteria.name: Technical depth
selectionCriteria.description: Projects with real algorithms, engine design, worker pipelines, platform APIs, or meaningful architecture rank higher than simple UI exercises.

selectionCriteria.name: Portfolio signal
selectionCriteria.description: Featured work should quickly communicate judgment, ownership, polish, and the ability to ship complete tools.

selectionCriteria.name: User value
selectionCriteria.description: A stronger project solves a specific workflow pain, has clear users, and explains why the implementation choices matter.

selectionCriteria.name: Demo quality
selectionCriteria.description: Live static demos and visual previews get priority because they let visitors verify the work immediately.

projects.name: Casino Cheat Sheet
projects.headline: A browser-only casino analysis suite built around exact combinatorics and evaluator-backed poker equity tools.
projects.description: Combines rule-driven analyzers for roulette, baccarat, craps, blackjack, video poker, three-card poker, and pai gow with poker equity tooling for Hold'em, Omaha, and seven-card stud. Heavy analyzers run in browser workers so the UI stays responsive on GitHub Pages.
projects.whyFeatured: This is the strongest portfolio signal: static deployment constraints, serious math, multi-page product thinking, and separated engine/frontend architecture.

projects.name: LinkedIn Puzzle Solver
projects.headline: A collection of browser solvers for LinkedIn's daily puzzle games.
projects.description: Solves Zip, Tango, Queens, Patches, and Mini Sudoku with puzzle-specific validation, constraint propagation, and pruned backtracking. The interface makes clues, generated cells, and impossible states visible so the solver feels inspectable rather than magical.
projects.whyFeatured: It makes algorithms tangible, has a clean static deployment story, and shows careful interaction design around complex state.

projects.name: Farkle Lab
projects.headline: A playable Farkle game paired with exact expected-value strategy tools.
projects.description: Runs human-vs-CPU games in the browser, highlights legal scoring choices, precomputes expected-value tables for one through six dice, and includes a state advisor for custom score situations. It is part game, part explainable decision engine.
projects.whyFeatured: It turns probability into a product experience and shows applied math without needing a backend.

projects.name: Spotify Manager
projects.headline: A GitHub Pages-friendly playlist editor with PKCE auth and analysis workflows.
projects.description: Handles Spotify OAuth in the browser, loads playlist metadata, supports sorting, filtering, deduping, custom ordering, outlier detection, transition diagnostics, and playlist export. It treats a static host like a serious application surface.
projects.whyFeatured: It demonstrates careful static OAuth, data-table UX, and local-first workflow design.

projects.name: Video Stabbot
projects.headline: A professional video stabilization desktop app with multiple motion-analysis engines.
projects.description: Combines Electron, FFmpeg vidstab, OpenCV feature tracking, and RAFT optical flow behind a polished UI with dependency detection, progress reporting, drag-and-drop input, GPU encoder detection, and configurable stabilization parameters.
projects.whyFeatured: It is visually interesting and technically ambitious across desktop, media processing, Python integration, and AI-assisted motion analysis.

projects.name: Trip Planner
projects.headline: A route-aware itinerary planner that ranks stops against the trip timeline.
projects.description: Plans meal, coffee, rest, scenic, hike, attraction, gas, EV charging, and surprise stops using slot fit, detour cost, daylight, open-hours, review quality, and preference fit. It keeps a demo mode fully client-side while allowing Google Maps enhancement.
projects.whyFeatured: It shows product architecture under static hosting constraints and exposes ranking decisions rather than hiding them.

projects.name: Regex Isolator
projects.headline: A zero-dependency regex workbench for testing patterns against large text.
projects.description: Uses Python's standard library to provide live or manual matching, highlighting, click-to-jump results, flags, presets, file I/O, and a cache/unload mode for huge inputs.

projects.name: Tab Volume Adjuster
projects.headline: A focused Manifest V3 extension for per-site tab volume and mono audio.
projects.description: Captures tab audio through an offscreen document, persists settings by hostname, lists audible tabs, and provides settings for volume step size, max volume, persistence, and popup behavior.

projects.name: Chess.com Lichess Link
projects.headline: A one-click PGN bridge from Chess.com games to Lichess imports.
projects.description: Detects supported Chess.com pages, waits for PGN readiness, opens Lichess import with a URL-hash token, and fills the import form in-page without clipboard access or API tokens.

projects.name: Amazon Bestseller Extractor
projects.headline: A scoped extension for extracting Amazon Best Sellers Rank data from product pages.
projects.description: Reads BSR categories from supported storefronts, displays the strongest rank as a toolbar badge, lists category links in a compact popup, and avoids broad host permissions.

projects.name: Instagram Saver
projects.headline: A media downloader for Instagram pages available in the user's browser session.
projects.description: Supports posts, reels, stories, highlights, profile batches, metadata sidecars, batch reports, folder templates, pacing controls, and checkpointed full-profile crawls.

projects.name: Steam OneNote Sync
projects.headline: A bidirectional sync bridge between local Steam game notes and Microsoft OneNote.
projects.description: Normalizes both systems into a canonical note model, previews push/pull/sync writes, tracks OneNote pages with sidecar state, and projects rich OneNote content back to Steam's safer subset.

projects.name: PATH Manager
projects.headline: A safer Windows PATH editor with diagnostics, backups, and diff previews.
projects.description: Turns PATH editing into a reorderable UI with user/system scopes, missing-path cleanup, duplicate detection, command shadowing, risk warnings, backup snapshots, and admin-aware saving.

projects.name: Lossless Scaling Wrapper
projects.headline: A Windows launcher that starts Lossless Scaling, launches a game, and restores focus.
projects.description: Designed for Steam launch options, the wrapper finds Lossless Scaling, starts the target game command, minimizes the scaling window, foregrounds the game, and returns the game's exit code.

projects.name: Chrome Extension Code Viewer
projects.headline: A local extension explorer with permission risk scoring and entry-point maps.
projects.description: Scans installed Chrome extensions, resolves localized manifest names, maps popup/background/content-script entry points, scores risky permissions, and can enrich entries with store metadata.

projects.name: Autoclicker
projects.headline: A compact always-on-top autoclicker built only with Python standard libraries.
projects.description: Supports left, right, and middle clicks, configurable intervals, global hotkeys, a custom dark title bar, and a screen-corner fail-safe.

projects.name: 2048 Game
projects.headline: A Python implementation of the 2048 tile-merging game.
projects.description: A compact game project focused on grid state, tile movement, merge rules, and responsive input handling.

projects.name: GitHub Profile Config
projects.headline: The profile README and GitHub profile configuration repository.
projects.description: A supporting repository for keeping the public GitHub profile consistent with the portfolio narrative and current technical focus.
